name: IDOR: Profile Viewer
learningObjectives: Understand how Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) occur when an application trusts a client-supplied identifier without checking whether the current user is allowed to access it
Practice identifying IDOR by manipulating an identifier in a request (URL, body, or query parameter) and observing whether access control is enforced
Understand the standard fix: enforce object-level authorization on every request, and consider using indirect reference maps instead of exposing raw database IDs
hints: Every request that fetches a profile includes some kind of identifier. What happens if you change just that value while keeping your own session cookie?
The app checks 'is someone logged in,' not 'does this ID belong to that someone.' Try incrementing or decrementing the identifier you see in your own profile URL.
description: A small profile-viewing app lets a logged-in user view their own profile at /profile/<id>. The application authenticates the request, but never checks whether the id in the URL actually belongs to the logged-in user. Your goal: log in as one user, then use the app to read another user's private profile data without their credentials.
